subject: science
question_text: What is meant by a pure substance?
answer_text: Substance having single type of particles is known as pure substance. For example: Hydrogen, Water etc., are pure. Note: All elements and compounds are considered to be pure.
final_answer: Thus, a pure substance consists of a single type of particle.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of the definition of a pure substance.

subject: science
question_text: List the points of differences between homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures.
answer_text: Homogeneous mixture: Its constituent particles cannot be seen easily. There are no visible boundaries of separation. Its constituents cannot be easily separated. Examples: Alloys, solution of salt in water. Heterogeneous mixture: Its constituent particles can be seen easily. Have visible boundaries of separation. Its constituents can be separated by simple methods. Examples: Mixture of sand and common salt, mixture of sand and water.
final_answer: Therefore, homogeneous mixtures are uniform, while heterogeneous mixtures are not.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding and comparison of two concepts.

subject: science
question_text: How are sol, solution and suspension different from each other?
answer_text: Solution: A true solution is homogeneous, has no Tyndall effect, and solute particles cannot be filtered. Examples: Sea water, alloys. Sol (colloidal solution): A colloidal solution is heterogeneous, shows Tyndall effect, and cannot be separated by ordinary filter paper. Examples: Milk of magnesia, fog. Suspension: A suspension is also heterogeneous, shows Tyndall effect, and can be separated by filter paper. Examples: Mixture of sand in water.
final_answer: Thus, solutions are homogeneous, while sols and suspensions are heterogeneous with distinct properties.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding and differentiating between three types of mixtures.

subject: science
question_text: How will you separate a mixture containing kerosene and petrol (difference in their boiling points is more than 25°C), which are miscible with each other?
answer_text: Simple distillation is the method which can separate the mixture of kerosene and petrol.
final_answer: Thus, simple distillation is the appropriate method for separation.

subject: science
question_text: Name the technique to separate (i) Butter from curd (ii) Salt from sea water (iii) Camphor from salt.
answer_text: (i) By using centrifugation method, butter can be separated from curd. (ii) By using evaporation method, salt from sea water can be separated. (iii) Camphor from salt can be separated by sublimation method.
final_answer: Therefore, the techniques are centrifugation, evaporation, and sublimation respectively.

subject: science
question_text: What types of mixtures are separated by the technique of crystallisation?
answer_text: Crystallisation method can be used for the purification of those mixtures which contain insoluble and/or soluble impurities and have crystalline nature.
final_answer: Thus, crystallisation is suitable for mixtures with impurities and crystalline nature.

parts.part_text: What mass of potassium nitrate would be needed to produce a saturated solution of potassium nitrate in 50 grams of water at 313 K?
parts.answer_text: Mass of potassium nitrate needed to produce its saturated solution in 100 g of water at 313 K = 62 g. Therefore, for 50 g of water, it would be 31 g.

parts.part_text: Pragya makes a saturated solution of potassium chloride in water at 353 K and leaves the solution to cool at room temperature. What would she observe as the solution cools? Explain.
parts.answer_text: As the solution cools, crystals of potassium chloride are formed. This happens as solubility of solid decreases with decreasing temperature.
parts.final_answer: Crystals of potassium chloride will form as the solution cools.

parts.part_text: Find the solubility of each salt at 293 K. Which salt has the highest solubility at this temperature?
parts.answer_text: Solubility of each salt at 293 K: Potassium nitrate 32 g, Sodium chloride 36 g, Potassium chloride 35 g, Ammonium chloride 37 g. Ammonium chloride has the maximum solubility (37 g per 100 g of water) at 293 K.
parts.final_answer: Ammonium chloride has the highest solubility at this temperature.

parts.part_text: What is the effect of change of temperature on the solubility of a salt?
parts.answer_text: The solubility of a solid salt decreases with decrease in temperature while it increases with rise in temperature.
parts.final_answer: Solubility increases with temperature and decreases with cooling.
